tasks.short: Watch security alarms, assess alerts and record incidents for follow-up.

steps.what: Watch the {OTHER} security alarm console for new alerts.
Check alarm location, status and response instructions in the {DOCS}.
Assess the alert and decide whether security staff must investigate.
Record the alert and chosen response in the incident log.

tasks.design: Configure notifications in the {OTHER} security alarm system and join events to site maps and approved procedures from the {DOCS}. A small dashboard on the {WORKFLOW} shows the original alert and prefills an incident record; the operator assesses the situation and confirms the response record.
tasks.previous_blocker: Alarm consoles, site instructions and incident logs were separate. Connecting them required site-specific access and maintenance.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing alert configuration and event interfaces can handle much of the work. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of building the remaining lookup and record integration.
tasks.still_hard: Sensor faults, incomplete location data and uncertain physical conditions remain hard. The integration must preserve original alerts and work during outages.
tasks.human_edge: The operator interprets site context, recognises uncertainty and seeks a physical check. Security staff decide what action is safe on site.

ambition.what: A shift-start review of recurring alarm faults

tasks.altitude: The week contains less watching and copying, with more attention to active incidents and recurring faults. The operator can recommend maintenance priorities; authority to reset alarms or direct emergency response does not expand.

reach.role: first-line supervisor of office and administrative support workers
reach.task: Review incident handoffs and recurring alarm faults.
reach.learn: Learn incident review, fault patterns and the site's escalation responsibilities.

evidence.claim: Alarm notifications, event lookups and incident records can use deterministic configuration and integration.
AI that evaluates emergency calls or sets dispatch priority falls within the cited high-risk category; this design does neither.
GDPR applies to identifiable incident records. Employee consultation and monitoring requirements depend on national rules.
In the Netherlands, employee monitoring arrangements may require works council consent.

assumptions: Monitoring mainly uses a security alarm console. This differs from the prior's large in-person share.
The alarm system already detects events; the proposed change connects notifications and context.
The operator does not replace a dedicated security control room.
Time shares are illustrative task estimates, not measured customer data.
unknowns: Which alarm types the operator monitors and which require continuous human attention.
Whether the alarm system supports reliable event access and notifications.
Who may acknowledge, reset or close each alarm type.
Which national consultation rules and existing agreements apply.
Whether the current incident log is electronic or on paper.
research_questions: Can event access preserve alarm ordering, timestamps and outage behaviour?
Which console notifications can be configured without custom code?
What fallback preserves monitoring when the integration fails?
new_work: Maintain site maps, alarm identifiers and procedure links.
Test notification delivery and outage fallback.
Review recurring faults without turning incident data into employee scoring.

tasks.short: Contact security staff by radio or telephone and confirm they received the incident details.

steps.what: Find the responsible security contact in the duty roster.
Check incident details and choose the required escalation.
Contact security staff through the {OTHER} radio system or the {TELEPHONY}.
Enter acknowledgement and follow-up details in the incident log.

tasks.design: A deterministic lookup on the {WORKFLOW} combines the incident record with the duty roster from the {DOCS} and displays the contact and briefing fields. The operator chooses the escalation and makes the radio or {TELEPHONY} call, then records acknowledgement through a short form with automatic timestamps.
tasks.previous_blocker: Duty rosters and incident records were separate, while radio conversations offered little structured data. The main work still required a person to exchange urgent information.
tasks.enabler_now: A small roster lookup and incident form can now be built cheaply. They reduce preparation and paperwork without needing speech interpretation or automated dispatch.
tasks.still_hard: Unreachable staff, noisy radios and changing incident conditions still require live coordination. Accurate acknowledgement cannot be inferred from a call being connected.
tasks.human_edge: The operator confirms understanding, adapts the briefing and notices when the response is inadequate.
tasks.altitude: The operator spends slightly less time finding contacts and writing logs. Most of this task remains live coordination, and decision rights do not change.

reach.task: Maintain the current duty contact list and cover incident handoffs.
reach.learn: Learn roster ownership, acknowledgement standards and escalation fallback.

evidence.claim: Structured contact lookup and timestamped acknowledgement forms need no model loop.
The emergency-call classification and dispatch-priority category supports keeping those decisions outside this automation.
GDPR applies to identifiable incident and contact records; employee consultation depends on national rules.
The Netherlands has works council consent requirements for employee monitoring arrangements.

assumptions: Security contacts may include contracted staff, so the live call has external-action authority.
The operator records receipt explicitly rather than assuming a connected call was understood.
The prior correctly favours human judgement, but radio and telephone are better represented as paper_phone than in_person.
Incident recording uses structured fields and does not require routine audio recording.
unknowns: Who owns and updates the duty roster.
Whether security staff are internal, contracted or both.
Which communication channels and fallback numbers are approved.
What information may be included in incident records.
Which consultation requirements apply to the proposed records.
research_questions: Can roster changes reach the lookup before the next shift?
Which fields let staff record acknowledgement quickly without losing essential detail?
Can the form remain usable during a network outage?
new_work: Maintain fallback contacts and roster freshness checks.
Enter acknowledgement and unresolved follow-up details.

tasks.short: Collect caller details, complete a sales order form and pass it to the sales team.

steps.what: Ask the caller for order details and note the request.

loop.input: Caller speech during a fixed order-intake dialogue.
loop.output: Draft customer, item, quantity, delivery and contact fields.
loop.check: Validate field types; read back items, quantities and delivery details; require explicit confirmation.
loop.stop: At most two clarification attempts per required field and a five-minute automated intake budget; transfer unresolved intake to the operator.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free speech contains corrections and variable wording. A structured form remains cheaper where the caller can use one.

steps.what: Find the customer in the {CRM} and items in the {ERP}.
Enter customer, item, quantity and delivery fields in the {ERP} order form.
Check the form and call back when required details are missing.
Send the completed form to the sales team through the {EMAIL}.

tasks.design: Configure a draft-order form and sales queue in the {ERP}, with customer lookup from the {CRM} and deterministic field validation. A bounded speech intake on the {TELEPHONY} drafts fields for operator confirmation, while the {WORKFLOW} routes checked forms to the sales coordinator. The sales coordinator approves order acceptance before any customer commitment or fulfilment instruction.
tasks.previous_blocker: Spoken requests did not arrive as validated fields, and customer and item data required separate lookups. Draft entry and sales approval were often connected through a mailbox.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing forms and queues can handle validation and handoff. Bounded speech extraction can fill a fixed schema, while AI-assisted coding reduces the cost of connecting supported interfaces.
tasks.still_hard: Ambiguous items, negotiated prices and uncertain delivery promises need sales judgement. Customer matching must prevent one caller's information appearing in another customer's order.
tasks.human_edge: The operator notices hesitation and misunderstandings. The sales coordinator resolves commercial exceptions and accepts the order.

ambition.what: Telephone order intake for customers unable to use the online form

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from retyping to checking uncertain requests and resolving missing details. The operator can return incomplete drafts for clarification, but gains no authority to change prices or accept orders.

reach.task: Resolve order-entry exceptions before sales acceptance.
reach.learn: Learn catalogue identifiers, customer verification and the limits of delivery promises.

evidence.claim: Existing records forms and workflows can validate draft orders and route them for sales approval.
Speech-to-order-field extraction is a proposed bounded loop; the digest provides no documented order-entry case.
Callers interacting with AI must receive the required disclosure, and synthetic audio has marking requirements.
GDPR requires an appropriate basis, purpose and retention policy for identifiable caller data.
In the Netherlands, employee recording or monitoring arrangements may require works council consent.

assumptions: The operator prepares a draft order; the sales team accepts it.
A mid-size company commonly uses an order screen rather than only a document template.
Existing supported lookup and form configuration is sufficient for routine fields.
The intake retains necessary fields rather than keeping audio by default.
The prior's high automation potential fits form entry, but live exceptions and commercial approval remain.
unknowns: Whether the current form is in the {ERP}, a document or paper.
Which customer and item lookup interfaces are available.
Which fields, prices and delivery terms require sales approval.
Caller languages, call quality and accessibility needs.
The applicable lawful basis, retention period and national consultation requirements.
research_questions: Can the {ERP} keep drafts separate from accepted orders and fulfilment?
How accurately does bounded intake capture item identifiers and quantities in supported languages?
Can caller confirmation work without retaining audio?
Which native form and queue configuration avoids custom integration?
new_work: Review extracted order fields and ambiguous matches.
Resolve missing details and commercial exceptions.
Maintain catalogue mappings and validation rules.
Check that drafts cannot trigger fulfilment.
Maintain AI disclosure and caller-data retention settings.

tasks.short: Answer routine business questions from reference files and refer uncertain requests to the responsible staff.

steps.what: Ask what the caller needs and establish which business their question concerns.
Find the relevant business reference file in the {DOCS}.
Choose the relevant information and check whether it answers the question.

loop.input: Caller question and current, caller-visible passages for the identified business.
loop.output: An approved answer passage with its source, or a handoff reason.
loop.check: Require a valid source identifier, exact approved wording, permitted topic and current source version; reject conflicts and unsupported requests.
loop.stop: One selection attempt and at most one clarification, within ten seconds; otherwise transfer to a person.
loop.why_not_simpler: Exact question mappings handle common FAQs first. A bounded semantic selection handles varied wording across prose reference files.

steps.what: Give the caller the answer and explain any stated limits.
Clarify unresolved questions and transfer the caller to responsible staff.

tasks.design: Configure routine questions and approved answers in the {TELEPHONY}, using current reference material from the {DOCS}. Exact FAQ matches run directly; a bounded loop selects approved passages for other routine wording, and deterministic checks permit only current, caller-visible answers. Unresolved, sensitive or urgent requests transfer to the operator without automated emergency classification.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reference files were written for staff and lacked clear publication scope, ownership and expiry dates. Ordinary call menus could route callers but could not handle varied question wording.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing phone features already answer approved questions and route calls. Bounded semantic selection can cover a limited set of prose files, provided content is curated and checked.
tasks.still_hard: Stale information, ambiguous business identity and implied promises can produce harmful answers. Reliable service depends on content ownership, language support and a reachable human fallback.
tasks.human_edge: The operator recognises distress, ambiguity and requests that need personal context. Staff can explain exceptions without pretending the reference file settles them.

ambition.what: After-hours answers about opening hours, locations and published contact routes

tasks.altitude: The week shifts toward unresolved enquiries and improving weak reference material. The operator can propose answer changes; the business content owner retains publication authority.

reach.task: Turn recurring caller questions into approved reference answers.
reach.learn: Learn source checking, publication scope and concise wording.

reach.task: Handle enquiries that need account context or exceptions.
reach.learn: Learn verification requirements and when routine information becomes a customer-specific commitment.

evidence.claim: Approved question answering and call routing are available in existing phone software, including Dutch support in the cited product.
Existing receptionist software can answer from uploaded files and transfer callers; supported languages vary.
A cited voice service supports FAQ answering and routing to people or departments.
Callers must receive the required AI disclosure, and synthetic audio has marking requirements.
The cited AI transparency provisions apply from August 2026.
The cited chatbot case illustrates that incorrect automated business advice can create liability.
GDPR applies to identifiable caller data, and employee consultation requirements vary under national rules.

assumptions: Automatic answers are limited to approved public information, without account-specific advice or commercial commitments.
A business content owner approves answer material before publication; individual routine calls need no operator approval.
The company has a manageable set of current reference files.
Phone conversations are represented as paper_phone, correcting the prior's large in-person share.
The retained human exception step is a share of overall task time, not an activity in every call.
unknowns: Which questions are common and safe to answer automatically.
Who approves each business's reference material.
Which languages callers need and the current {TELEPHONY} supports.
Whether files contain internal information that must be excluded.
Human fallback coverage and after-hours escalation arrangements.
The lawful basis, retention policy and applicable national consultation rules.
research_questions: Can existing {TELEPHONY} configuration meet the requirements without a custom loop?
Can the answer mechanism enforce exact approved passages and business-specific access?
How often do paraphrases, names and noisy calls cause incorrect answer selection?
Does the implementation provide the required AI disclosure and synthetic-audio marking?
new_work: Approve, version and expire reference answers.
Review unsupported questions and incorrect selections.
Maintain permitted topics and business-specific access.
Test language coverage and human transfers.
Check AI disclosure, retention settings and fallback availability.

role.altitude: The operator spends less time watching screens, searching files and copying caller details. The role concentrates on uncertain enquiries, security coordination and checking drafts; safety decisions and commercial acceptance remain with the responsible people.
reach: Customer service representatives: resolve order and enquiry exceptions.
Receptionists and information clerks: maintain contact routes and cover handoffs.
Correspondence clerks: prepare source-backed reference answers.
First-line supervisors of office and administrative support workers: review recurring faults and service handoffs.
skills_to_grow: Testing call routing and outage fallback
role.ambitious_version: An operator who coordinates difficult live contacts and improves the information and handoffs behind routine calls, while offering approved after-hours business information and accessible telephone order intake.
